external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A person who browses and orders socks through the mobile app and receives fax confirmations.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application customers use to browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app, storing customer information and forwarding orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that processes orders, writes delivery addresses to a flat file, and sends dispatch notes to the fax gateway.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that receives dispatch notes, dials the number stored against the order, and faxes customer confirmations.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation
processes.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: A database containing customer names, addresses, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database ... [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether ... the flat file [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: spreadsheet
data_stores.description: A spreadsheet containing the marketing catalogue, with macros that change prices and product copy through SQL statements to the web API.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browsing and ordering interaction with the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: talk to API
data_flows.description: The mobile app communicates with the web API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keep customers
data_flows.description: The web API keeps customer information in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: Customer name, address, and payment card information

data_flows.name: hand order over
data_flows.description: The web API hands an order over to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address into the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway
data_flows.data_description: Dispatch note containing customer name and address

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.
data_flows.data_description: Confirmation containing customer name and address

data_flows.name: change catalogue
data_flows.description: Spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: customer device
trust_boundaries.description: The customer-controlled device hosting the mobile app.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

trust_boundaries.name: Sokify internal
trust_boundaries.description: The internal Sokify environment containing the web API, databases, SIMS, fax gateway, and marketing spreadsheet.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app runs on a customer-controlled device.
assumptions.basis: The text describes customers using the mobile app but does not name its hosting device; a mobile app is inferred to run on the customer's device.

assumptions.assumption: The customer is in the customer device trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The customer uses the mobile app and is treated as the controlling party for the customer-side device boundary.

assumptions.assumption: The customer device is a tenant boundary.
assumptions.basis: The customer controls the device, making it a zone controlled by a different party from Sokify.

assumptions.assumption: The Sokify components described as being in the office or belonging to Sokify share an internal network boundary.
assumptions.basis: The text places the marketing laptop in the office and refers to the systems as Sokify's; the boundary is inferred as a same-party network zone.
It contains customer names and addresses, plus payment-card information.
